headline: The world's invisible burden
dek: More than a billion people live with mental disorders. The sharper global divide is not whether mental illness exists, but whether care systems have the money, people and services to respond.

facts.label: people were living with a mental disorder in 2021
facts.detail: WHO reports an age-standardized prevalence of 13.6% — nearly one in seven people worldwide.

facts.label: age-standardized global prevalence in 2021
facts.detail: A modeled GBD estimate, not a count of diagnosed cases or a national wellbeing score.

facts.label: people living with anxiety disorders in 2021
facts.detail: WHO's table uses the GBD category that includes anxiety disorders and PTSD.

facts.label: people living with depressive disorders in 2021
facts.detail: The category includes major depressive disorder and dysthymia.

facts.label: DALYs attributed to mental disorders in 2021
facts.detail: GBD 2021 gives a 95% uncertainty interval of 117–198 million; almost all of this burden was nonfatal disability (YLDs).

facts.label: of all global DALYs in 2021
facts.detail: 95% uncertainty interval: 4.3–6.5%.

facts.detail: WHO reports roughly 1.1–2.4 per 100,000 in low- and lower-middle-income settings versus 67.2 in high-income settings.
